attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: A firm retrospective assertion that long-term adoption, as opposed to experimentation, was modest by July 2024. The 'vs mere experimentation' qualifier is kept, and the revised wording no longer overgeneralises.

contract.note: The plain reading (sustained consumer and production use stayed limited compared with trials) is fair and ordinary. 'Modest' and 'long-term' have no thresholds, so the result depends on that reading and on retention data that is not in the packet.

evidence.note: Reuters Institute survey from March–April 2024: low daily ChatGPT use and much one-off experimentation. This leans toward the claim, but it is a cross-sectional snapshot and does not measure retention.

McKinsey survey from February–March 2024: 65% of respondents' organisations regularly use gen AI in at least one function. This cuts against the claim, but it is self-reported, not representative of all firms, and not evidence of retention or how long deployments lasted.

reviews.rationale: The two in-period surveys point in different directions: low routine consumer use against widespread reported regular business use. Neither measures long-term retention or how long production use lasted, which is what the contract requires. The packet itself records this gap. The evidence does not settle whether lasting adoption was modest.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Reading 'GPT-5 is still a no show' as 'GPT-5 had not been publicly released as of July 2024' is faithful.

contract.note: Reading 'no show' as no public release is the ordinary meaning. Excluding models released under other names is fair.

evidence.note: OpenAI's official release notes list GPT-4o mini on 18 July 2024, not GPT-5. This is a company disclosure, but the chronology it records is consistent with no GPT-5 release.
Tom's Guide, 2 July 2024: it treats GPT-5 as a future model and GPT-4o as the current release. Sidebar links on the page come from later retrieval and do not matter here.
OpenAI introduced GPT-5 on 7 August 2025, before the evaluation date. It falls outside the period, but it corroborates that GPT-5 was not released in July 2024.

reviews.rationale: Contemporary reporting from early July 2024 treats GPT-5 as forthcoming. OpenAI's release history for July shows GPT-4o mini, and GPT-5 was introduced only in August 2025. Nothing in the packet shows a GPT-5 release on or before 24 July 2024.

attribution.note: Marcus's own retrospective assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: 'All that has borne out' firmly asserts that every January warning was confirmed: plateau, adoption, tensions, profits and moat. Some of those original warnings were hedged, but the retrospective assertion itself is firm.

contract.note: Mostly fair, but the result depends on choices Marcus did not supply. Plateau is defined as 'meaningful improvement', a lower bar than his 'significantly better', and profit is assessed on a realized April–June quarter that the evaluator chose.

evidence.note: Jan Leike's departure thread of 17 May 2024 describes long disagreement with leadership. This supports the internal-tensions part. It is personal testimony reproduced on a third-party site.

OpenAI's own account of GPT-4o: it matches GPT-4 Turbo on English text and code, with gains in vision, non-English text, speed and cost. Whether that counts as 'significantly better' depends on interpretation, and the source is a company self-report.
OpenAI–Apple partnership announced 10 June 2024, with integration still to come. It does not show a durable moat or the absence of one.

reviews.rationale: Only internal tensions is supported. The plateau part is contested: the company's own account shows parity on English text and code, with gains elsewhere, and whether that is a plateau depends on reading. There is no realized April–June profit or loss evidence. Neither adoption relative to valuation nor durable moat is settled. The five-part assertion cannot be confirmed or clearly refuted from the packet.
